objective: At the owner's request ('Can we do all 3?', approving option (b) of FOUR-PLACE-20261031-001's recommendation): complete the four-place picture with the knots that prefer a value. Catalogue every four-place knot on signed 4-regular 4-uniform systems; for each class decide whether it never fails, builds a link (and is NP-complete on 4-regular systems), or has a polynomial count; state whether any four-place knot can be mutually selecting, and isolate what stays open. No time constraints.
status: Complete 2026-11-01: the four-place picture for every law. Four-place knots are the relations whose excluded states form a non-empty independent set of the 4-cube (742 relations, 20 classes). Parity's count is polynomial; the clause and not-all-equal never fail; twelve classes (two value-free, ten preferring a value) build links and are NP-complete on 4-regular systems, ten of them through a three-point core that realizes the twelve class; five weak classes (two or three excluded states) never failed in any search. So, unless NP-complete problems are polynomial, a mutually selecting four-place knot would have to be one of those five; three remains the only arity found with a law that fails and stays rigid. Recommendation: Continue as approved (composition, then the note)
stop_rule: Stop when every class is settled (never fails, NP-complete via a link, or polynomial count) or isolated as open with exact evidence; a class with non-empty recognisable failures and a hard count would be recorded as a finding.
title: Four-place laws that prefer a value
